stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: To help a depleted grouper population recover, regulators closed one section of a Caribbean reef to all fishing. Within three years, grouper counts inside the closed section had nearly doubled. The fishing boats that once worked that section did not leave the area, however; they moved to the reef's open edges, which they now fish far more heavily than before. Thus, an unintended effect of the closure has been ______
choices: a decline in the grouper population inside the closed section.
an increase in the total number of boats fishing the region.
greater fishing pressure on the parts of the reef left open.
a shift among local crews toward species other than grouper.
explanation: The closure's goal was to protect fish, and it worked inside the closed section. The passage then says the same boats moved to the open edges and now fish them more heavily. The unintended effect is the extra pressure on the reef that is still open.

A.why: You placed the harm on the side the policy protected. The passage says grouper counts inside the closed section nearly doubled.

B.why: The passage says the existing boats moved. It never says more boats arrived, so you added a step the text doesn't support.

D.why: Nothing in the passage says crews switched species. They kept fishing, just in a different place.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Inspectors can examine a suspension bridge's deck and towers simply by looking at them, so those parts are checked often. The thousands of steel wires bundled inside the bridge's main cables are a different matter. Those wires are wrapped and sealed, so checking them for corrosion means unwrapping a section of cable. That process is so costly that it is done only rarely. As a result, there is a disparity between ______
choices: the cost of building a suspension bridge and the cost of maintaining its deck.
how often a bridge's visible parts are checked and how often its cable wires are.
the strength of the steel cable wires and the strength of the bridge's towers.
how quickly the cable wires corrode and how quickly the deck's steel corrodes.
explanation: The passage contrasts parts that are easy to see and checked often (the deck and towers) with cable wires that are hard to reach and checked rarely. The disparity is in how often each is inspected.

A.why: You paired the wrong two things. The passage never discusses construction costs. Its contrast is about how often parts get inspected.

C.why: The passage says nothing about how strong the cables or towers are. This pair isn't the contrast the text sets up.

D.why: The passage mentions checking for corrosion but never compares corrosion rates. You went beyond what it establishes.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many people assume that how well a vaccine protects depends only on the vaccine itself. Immunologists point out, however, that the response a vaccine triggers can vary with the recipient's age. After receiving the same dose, older adults often produce fewer protective antibodies than younger adults do. Consequently, health agencies that give a single standard dose to every age group risk ______
choices: leaving younger recipients less protected than older recipients.
making the vaccine less effective for recipients of every age.
raising the cost of producing and distributing the vaccine.
leaving older recipients less protected than younger recipients.
explanation: The passage says older adults produce fewer antibodies from the same dose. So when everyone gets one standard dose, older recipients end up less protected than younger ones.

A.why: You reversed the two groups. The passage says older adults, not younger ones, respond more weakly to the same dose.

B.why: This is strength creep. The passage describes a weaker response in one age group only, not across every age.

C.why: Cost never comes up in the passage. The tension is between a uniform dose and responses that differ by age.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Woodcut can look like the simplest printmaking method: an artist carves a design into a wooden block, inks the raised surface, and presses it onto paper. Yet every cut into the wood is permanent. A single slip of the knife can ruin a block that took weeks to carve, and the mistake cannot be sanded away without damaging the lines around it. Woodcut thus involves a mismatch between ______
choices: the apparent simplicity of the method and the precision that carving demands.
the price of a good wooden block and the price of high-quality printing ink.
the time it takes to carve a block and the time it takes to print from it.
the precision that carving demands and the difficulty of finding good wood.
explanation: The passage opens by saying woodcut looks simple, then explains that each permanent cut makes the carving unforgiving. The mismatch is between how simple the method looks and how precise the carving has to be.

B.why: You paired the wrong two things. The passage never mentions what blocks or ink cost.

C.why: The passage says carving can take weeks, but it never says how long printing takes. You supplied the second half yourself.

D.why: Only the first half of this pair matches the passage. Nothing in it says good wood is hard to find, and the 'looks simple' side of the contrast is missing.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: To reduce congestion downtown, one city began charging a toll for cars entering its central district during weekday business hours. Traffic in the district fell sharply. However, many commuters began parking on residential streets just outside the toll zone and walking the rest of the way, filling curbs that residents had once relied on. The toll's unintended effect, then, was ______
choices: heavier traffic inside the central district during business hours.
more parking congestion in the neighborhoods bordering the zone.
a drop in the number of people who work in the central district.
lower toll revenue than city officials had originally projected.
explanation: The toll succeeded downtown, but commuters started parking just outside the zone and crowded the residential streets there. The unintended effect is the parking congestion in those bordering neighborhoods.

A.why: You placed the harm on the side the toll was meant to help. The passage says traffic in the district fell sharply.

C.why: Commuters still walk into the district, so nothing suggests fewer people work there. You added an assumption.

D.why: The passage gives no revenue figures or projections. You can't conclude anything about toll income.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: In 2019 a regional government required employers to offer health insurance to any employee working at least 30 hours a week. The goal was to extend coverage to part-time workers, who often had none. Some labour economists warned, however, that employers could avoid the new cost by keeping schedules at 29 hours or fewer. If that happened, the rule would have the unintended effect of ______
choices: raising insurance costs for employees who already worked full-time schedules.
reducing the hours available to the part-time workers it was meant to help.
encouraging employers to move most part-time staff into full-time positions.
removing health coverage from every part-time worker in the entire region.
explanation: The rule was meant to protect part-time workers. The economists' warning is that employers would cap shifts at 29 hours. That cap falls on part-time workers, so the rule would cut hours for the very group it was written to help. An unintended effect usually works against the policy's own goal, and this one does.

A.why: You picked a cost to full-time workers, but the passage never mentions them. The tension is between the rule's goal and its effect on part-time workers, not on a group it never targeted.

C.why: You reversed the warning. The economists expected employers to cut schedules to below 30 hours, not raise workers to full-time positions.

D.why: You jumped from 'could keep schedules short' to 'every part-time worker loses coverage.' Most of these workers had no coverage to lose, and 'every' goes far beyond a warning that something could happen.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: The Mercator projection, first published in 1569, preserves angles exactly, so a straight line on the map is a constant compass bearing. That made it ideal for navigation. To keep angles true, though, the projection stretches regions more and more as they get farther from the equator. Greenland appears roughly as large as Africa, even though Africa is about fourteen times larger. On a Mercator map, then, there is a disparity between ______
choices: the compass bearings a map shows and the bearings a ship actually follows.
how large high-latitude regions look and how much area they actually cover.
how useful the map was to sailors and how popular it became with the public.
the size of Greenland on the map and the number of people who live there.
explanation: The passage sets angles, which stay true, against areas, which get stretched far from the equator. The Greenland and Africa example shows the gap: regions at high latitudes look much bigger than they really are. The disparity is between how big they look and how big they are.

A.why: You paired the wrong two things. The passage says Mercator keeps bearings exactly right, so map bearings and real bearings match. Area is what gets distorted.

C.why: You chose a contrast the passage never makes. It says nothing about how popular the map was with the public, and its contrast is about distortion, not reception.

D.why: You kept Greenland but paired it with population, which the passage never mentions. The comparison is map size against actual land area.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many runners hold long static stretches just before a race, believing this prepares their muscles to perform. However, sports scientists have found that holding a single stretch for more than sixty seconds can temporarily reduce how much force a muscle produces. Because sprinting depends on generating force quickly, sprinters who hold long stretches immediately before a race risk ______
choices: losing the flexibility that they hoped the stretching would build.
running more slowly in the race the routine was meant to prepare for.
suffering more muscle injuries than runners who never stretch at all.
producing extra force in the first seconds after they leave the blocks.
explanation: Runners stretch to prepare for the race, but the research says long stretches temporarily lower muscle force, and sprinting depends on force. So the routine meant to help can slow sprinters down in the race it was supposed to prepare them for.

A.why: You picked a cost to flexibility, but the passage says nothing about stretching reducing flexibility. The effect it reports is on muscle force.

C.why: You added a step. The passage reports lower force, not more injuries, and it never compares stretchers with runners who skip stretching.

D.why: You reversed the finding. Long stretches reduce force, so 'extra force' is the opposite of what the passage reports.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: In much Baroque music, the keyboard player's part was written as just one bass line, with small numbers printed above some notes. On the page it can look sparse, almost unfinished. Yet those numbers only told players which chords to build. The players had to make up full harmonies on the spot, choosing voicings and rhythms as the music moved. For a continuo player, there was thus a disparity between ______
choices: how loudly the keyboard sounded and how loudly the melody instruments played.
how simple the written part appears and how much skill playing it required.
how complex the written part appears and how little effort playing it took.
how much the composers wrote down and how much the audience could follow.
explanation: The passage sets a sparse-looking page against a demanding job: players had to build full harmonies on the spot. The disparity is between how simple the part looks and how much skill it took to play.

A.why: You picked a contrast in volume, which the passage never brings up. The tension is between what is written and what the player has to supply.

C.why: You got both halves backwards. The passage says the part looks sparse and is hard to play, not that it looks complex and is easy.

D.why: You paired the wrong two things. The audience never appears in the passage. The contrast is between the written page and the player's work.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: To slow the decline of a shrinking aquifer, a state agency paid farmers to replace flood irrigation with drip systems, which deliver water directly to plant roots and waste far less. Hydrologists later found that in many districts, farmers used the water they saved to irrigate fields they had previously left dry. Total pumping in those districts rose. In those places, the subsidy appears to have had the unintended effect of ______
choices: lowering the crop yields of the farmers who had installed drip systems.
increasing the groundwater withdrawals that it had been designed to reduce.
shrinking the total area of farmland that relied on irrigation each season.
draining every aquifer in the state faster than before the program began.
explanation: The subsidy's goal was to protect the aquifer by cutting water use. Instead, farmers watered more land and total pumping went up. The unintended effect is the opposite of the goal: more groundwater withdrawn, not less.

A.why: You looked for harm to the farmers, but they were the ones paid, and the passage never mentions yields. The harm falls on the aquifer the program was meant to protect.

C.why: You reversed the finding. Farmers began irrigating fields they had left dry, so irrigated area grew rather than shrank.

D.why: Watch the quantifier. The passage limits the finding to 'many districts' and says the subsidy 'appears' to have had this effect. 'Every aquifer in the state' goes well beyond that.
